Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman confirmed today that relevant clues discovered in the macOS beta code show that Apple is designing its own game controller for the iPhone.

Apple currently sells some game controllers through the Apple Store, such as the Backbone One (pictured above) and the SteelSeries Nimbus+, and now hopes to capture a larger share of the iPhone game controller market.

The code discovery shows that two controllers are under development, with model identifiers T6502 and T1057 respectively. There is evidence in the code showing they are equipped with a D-Pad, analog sticks, haptic motors, and may have built-in accelerometers and gyroscopes to support motion controls. However, the specific exterior design of Apple's own game controller remains unclear.

Gurman believes that this accessory developed by Apple may ultimately be launched under the Beats brand, with the project overseen by Beats executives. Beats accessories are typically priced lower and use materials that are slightly cheaper than the high-end positioning of the Apple brand.

It is worth mentioning that users can connect MFi-certified game controllers to Apple devices, or use traditional console controllers such as the PlayStation DualShock and Xbox Wireless Controller.

Game controllers released under the Apple or Beats brand are also expected to improve the gaming ecosystem of the Apple TV 4K and increase user engagement with the increasingly sophisticated AAA games on iOS and Mac platforms.
